title: Perseroan Terbatas
scope_note: Cross-sector business-law review candidate for resource development and trading; sector tags are relevance, not verified applicability. Original 2007 company law, not a consolidated current text. Review UU6/2023, implementing rules and court decisions separately. Company formation and acquisition relevance does not establish mining permit transfer eligibility.

title: Penanaman Modal
scope_note: Cross-sector business-law review candidate for resource development and trading; sector tags are relevance, not verified applicability. Original 2007 investment law, not a consolidated current text. Review UU6/2023, sector-specific ownership rules and current investment implementation separately; no automatic incentive entitlement.

title: Jaminan Fidusia
scope_note: Cross-sector business-law review candidate for resource development and trading; sector tags are relevance, not verified applicability. Original fiduciary security statute. Review implementing rules and Constitutional Court decisions before interpreting enforcement or default; does not cover all forms of security or confer rights over a mining permit.

title: Kepailitan dan Penundaan Kewajiban Pembayaran Utang
identity_phrases: KEPAILITAN DAN PENUNDAAN KEWAJIBAN PEMBAYARAN UTANG
scope_note: Cross-sector business-law review candidate for resource development and trading; sector tags are relevance, not verified applicability. Original bankruptcy/PKPU statute. Later amendments and judicial interpretation need review, including financial-sector changes where relevant. Retrieval relevance is not a finding of priority or recoverability of a particular claim.

title: Arbitrase dan Alternatif Penyelesaian Sengketa
scope_note: Cross-sector business-law review candidate for resource development and trading; sector tags are relevance, not verified applicability. Original arbitration/ADR statute. Written dispute clauses, governing law, award recognition and current court procedure require separate review. Incoterms and private contracts are not Indonesian statutes.
